title: Correctness and size bound for tree emission
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $k$ be an AND or OR gate kind, and let $V_1,\ldots,V_r$ be lists of vertex indices. Let $G$ be an acyclic list of Boolean gates, and suppose every index in every $V_j$ is less than $n+|G|$. Emitting a tree of gates of kind $k$ for each list returns an extended acyclic gate list and one output index per list, each less than $n$ plus the length of the resulting gate list. On every Boolean input to the original $n$ vertices, the output values equal the values of the corresponding single gates of kind $k$ applied to the vertices in each original list. The resulting gate list has length at most $|G|+\sum_{j=1}^r c(|V_j|)$, where $c(0)=1$ and $c(s)=s-1$ for $s>0$; every appended gate has kind $k$, has distinct input indices, and reads at most two vertices.
hypotheses_covered: The gate kind is not negation (it is AND or OR)
The original gate list is acyclic
Every index in every input list is less than $n$ plus the original gate-list length
